Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. Per Hard Rule #2 the Implementer must either verify the authenticated `gh` login is in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (`gh api user --jq .login`, then the team membership call) or stop and get a named approving review before touching it. Do not start B0 on an unverified session.

Add a `cart` group to `detect-changes`'s allow-lists covering `overrides/app/pages/cart/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-item/**`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/**`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/cart/**`, `e2e/features/cart/**`. Note `e2e_homepage` is currently the **only** area group in the file — `testing.md`'s longer tag list is aspirational, so `cart` is the second, not the eighth.

### B1 — SFCC-315

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` | create | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | **modify** | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` | modify | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | modify | **Tier 2** | `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |

### B2 — SFCC-270 (copy-first)

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations

375	
376	Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.
377	
378	Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.
379	
380	**Pass criteria.**
381	1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*` shows exactly **one** emit site.
382	2. Each of the three copy strings is asserted verbatim in a test.
383	3. A Storybook `play` asserting a message queries `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing `testing.md`'s portal exception — Chakra toasts portal outside `canvasElement` and this is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`.
384	4. The SFCC-404 marker comment is present and names the ticket.
385	
386	#### Step 4.4 — `ZimmCartItemActions` + pending-item-across-auth
387	
388	**Changes.** Remove / Move to Wishlist as **underlined text links below the stepper** (SFCC-270 AC8, styled in B3's pass). Gap **24px**, not Figma's raw 25px — §11.10(4), snapped to the nearest tokenised value with a comment saying the design specified 25. Links `capitalize`, `textStyle="linkSm"`, `link/default` → `--zimm-color-text-default`.
389	
390	Note the actions are **not** inside base `product-item` — it receives them as a `secondaryActions` prop from its caller. So this molecule is supplied by the container, and we do not fight the base structure to inject it.
391	
392	Remove: item removed, drawer count decrements, totals update; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
393	
394	Wishlist, guest: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, **one hook instance**, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`. Per gate #5, this is a **deliberate override** of two sources that say "login page" (SFCC-272 AC7 and Confluence CAI-018), justified by consistency with the four other auth-drawer surfaces — record it as an override, not as an AC reading. The `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 paraphrase is the weaker justification and should not be the one cited.
395	
396	Pending item held in **React state** (covers email-code and create-account, where the page never unloads) **and** session storage (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first, fall back to storage, clear **both** together. Same **5-minute** age bound as the hook's own intent (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`), so a stale item cannot be resumed.
397	
398	Rejected and not to be revisited: one hook instance per line item (mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a drawer **per row** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed priority); adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent` (better long-term, but changes a shared hook with three existing call sites — raise separately).
399	
400	**Pass criteria — both links are interactive controls, so every state is named:**
401	1. Default: underlined, capitalized, `--zimm-color-text-default`, 24px gap, height 24 / py 4.
402	2. **Hover, focus-visible, active** inherited from `ZimmLink`'s recipe. Assert the focus-visible ring is **not identical** to default. Figma supplies only the `link/default` token for these links; inheritance is the resolution, annotated. If `ZimmLink` turns out to carry no focus treatment, that is an open question at that moment — not something to leave for the Tester.

   (`_app/`, `product-item/`, `theme/components/index.ts`), `@pwa-squad-a` and `@pwa-squad-b`;
   plus manually-requested reviewers for the three ungoverned files (`item-variant/`,
   `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, `useCartDrawer.ts`).
3. **Hard Rule #10 squarely engaged** — one change spanning Tier 1 CI/CD, Tier 2 Global Shell,
   Tier 2 Shared Product, Tier 2 theme registration, Tier 3 recipes and untiered code. Authorised:
   `marcelannavarro` verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` and repo `admin`, scope confirmed
   by him as the developer.
4. **Revert granularity is the whole cart.** If SIT surfaces a problem, the revert is all seven
   stories. Mitigated by the eighteen scoped commits, which allow a targeted revert instead.
5. **Zephyr build naming will be meaningless.** `computeBuildName.mjs` derives the name from a PR's

   dashboard. `e2e-browserstack-preview`'s `--grep` OR-joins all seven keys correctly, so scoping
   still works.

## PR body requirement

A ~60-file, seven-story PR is unverifiable without a body that maps **story → commits → files →
ACs**. That is `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s deliverable and it is real work — budget it rather than
discover it at the end. Note the recorded PR-body standard says *no SFCC key in the title* while
every recent PR carries one; settle which before opening.

389	### SFCC-795 — Cart Item UI Part 2 · the largest card
390	
391	Groups: default state (restates 270); stepper states (quantity 1 → `–` disabled/greyed; > 1 → both
392	enabled; at max → `+` disabled/greyed; fully OOS or unavailable → **both** disabled/greyed); error
393	state (red inline message beneath the stepper — OOS, Partially OOS, Unavailable, copy supplied);
394	promotional price ("Was $X" / "Now $Y" replacing standard price, plus a discount label beneath the
395	stepper e.g. "20% off applied"); warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. "Maximum purchase
396	quantity reached for this size"); responsive; and **11 accessibility ACs**.
397	
398	Decisions:
399	- **Overlap with 270/271/250 is intentional layering — build once, satisfy all.** This is the
400	  explicit reason for bundling. Consequence to accept: the ACs can't be signed off independently and
401	  Zephyr will count the same coverage from three keys.
402	- **Error states: presentation here, triggering logic elsewhere.** OOS / Partially OOS belong to
403	  SFCC-282, Unavailable to SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Tech design, Hazel's. Build the states
404	  prop-driven with stories; not provable end to end this sprint.
405	- **Promotional price: the was/now mechanism already exists.** Base `display-price` takes `priceData`
406	  with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` for the struck value, and already
407	  multiplies by quantity (`price={listPrice * quantity}`) so it is line-item aware. `cart.md` CAI-013
408	  confirms sale was/now is in scope and price-book sourced. **Only the discount label is new, and it
409	  is purely presentational** — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands.
410	  Note `display-price` has no override and is a shared SFCC internal; if Zimmermann styling is needed,
411	  use the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).
412	- **The 44×44px touch-target AC: annotate, do not escalate.** `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size is 24px,
413	  deliberately WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 (§2.11). The card asks for 44×44 while labelling it "WCAG 2.1 AA"
414	  — 44×44 is 2.1 **AAA**, and `AGENTS.md`'s standard is 2.2 AA. **Decision: inherit the existing 24px**,
415	  add an inline comment naming 795's AC and the mislabelling per the house pattern in §2.15, and add
416	  it to the UI designer's open list alongside the hover contrast (2.96:1) and inverse focus ring
417	  already there. Growing the atom would hit every icon button in the app.
418	
419	### SFCC-272 — Remove and Wishlist Actions · 8 ACs · 8 of 8 deliverable
420	
421	ACs — Remove (3): item removed with drawer count decrementing and totals updating; removing the last
422	item shows the empty state "as per SFCC-277"; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
423	Wishlist (5): authenticated qty 1 → moved, removed from cart, count decrements, totals update,
424	**page-level success banner** "[Product Name] has been moved to your wishlist"; authenticated qty > 1
425	→ all units removed, a single SKU saved, count decrements by the full quantity, same banner;
426	already in wishlist → **page-level error banner** "Selected product already exists in wishlist and
427	the item remains in the cart"; guest → redirected to login/registration, item stays in cart;
428	guest authenticates → returns, item moved, success banner at top of cart.
429	
430	Decisions:
431	- **Message surface: base Chakra toast as the interim.** All messages emitted through **one** handler
432	  so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. Use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not
433	  the base hook. Marker comment naming SFCC-404 at the emit site.
434	  - Consequence (good): with a toast, the message **behaviour and copy** are delivered, so what's
435	    deferred is presentation only, not functionality. AC6 — whose entire observable outcome is the
436	    error message — becomes deliverable.
437	  - Word the Jira comment as *"message behaviour and copy delivered; surface deferred to SFCC-404"*,
438	    **not** "AC met" — the ACs say page-level banner and a toast is not one.
439	  - There is no cart override today, so the toast is being *implemented*, not inherited. Not free.
440	  - Chakra toasts portal to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement`. A Storybook `play` asserting a
441	    message must use `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing the portal exception —
442	    `testing.md` sanctions that specifically and nowhere else.
443	- **Guest auth: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, not a page
444	  redirect.** AC7 says "redirected to the login/registration page"; the drawer is a deliberate
445	  divergence. Backed by `cart.md` §2 CAI-008 (*"prompted to log in first"*), which is
446	  drawer-compatible; §4 CAI-018's "redirected to login" is the looser wording.
447	- **Pending item across auth: one hook instance, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'.`** The cart holds the
448	  pending line item in **React state** (covers the email-code and create-account routes, where the
449	  page never unloads) **and session storage** (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first,
450	  fall back to storage, clear both. Use the same 5-minute age bound as the hook's own intent so a
451	  stale item can't be resumed.

### SFCC-795 — Cart Item UI Part 2 · the largest card

Groups: default state (restates 270); stepper states (quantity 1 → `–` disabled/greyed; > 1 → both
enabled; at max → `+` disabled/greyed; fully OOS or unavailable → **both** disabled/greyed); error
state (red inline message beneath the stepper — OOS, Partially OOS, Unavailable, copy supplied);
promotional price ("Was $X" / "Now $Y" replacing standard price, plus a discount label beneath the
stepper e.g. "20% off applied"); warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. "Maximum purchase
quantity reached for this size"); responsive; and **11 accessibility ACs**.

Decisions:
- **Overlap with 270/271/250 is intentional layering — build once, satisfy all.** This is the
  explicit reason for bundling. Consequence to accept: the ACs can't be signed off independently and
  Zephyr will count the same coverage from three keys.
- **Error states: presentation here, triggering logic elsewhere.** OOS / Partially OOS belong to
  SFCC-282, Unavailable to SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Tech design, Hazel's. Build the states
  prop-driven with stories; not provable end to end this sprint.
- **Promotional price: the was/now mechanism already exists.** Base `display-price` takes `priceData`
  with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` for the struck value, and already
  multiplies by quantity (`price={listPrice * quantity}`) so it is line-item aware. `cart.md` CAI-013
  confirms sale was/now is in scope and price-book sourced. **Only the discount label is new, and it
  is purely presentational** — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands.
  Note `display-price` has no override and is a shared SFCC internal; if Zimmermann styling is needed,
  use the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).
- **The 44×44px touch-target AC: annotate, do not escalate.** `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size is 24px,
  deliberately WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 (§2.11). The card asks for 44×44 while labelling it "WCAG 2.1 AA"
  — 44×44 is 2.1 **AAA**, and `AGENTS.md`'s standard is 2.2 AA. **Decision: inherit the existing 24px**,
  add an inline comment naming 795's AC and the mislabelling per the house pattern in §2.15, and add
  it to the UI designer's open list alongside the hover contrast (2.96:1) and inverse focus ring
  already there. Growing the atom would hit every icon button in the app.

### SFCC-272 — Remove and Wishlist Actions · 8 ACs · 8 of 8 deliverable

ACs — Remove (3): item removed with drawer count decrementing and totals updating; removing the last
item shows the empty state "as per SFCC-277"; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
Wishlist (5): authenticated qty 1 → moved, removed from cart, count decrements, totals update,
**page-level success banner** "[Product Name] has been moved to your wishlist"; authenticated qty > 1
→ all units removed, a single SKU saved, count decrements by the full quantity, same banner;
already in wishlist → **page-level error banner** "Selected product already exists in wishlist and
the item remains in the cart"; guest → redirected to login/registration, item stays in cart;
guest authenticates → returns, item moved, success banner at top of cart.

Decisions:
- **Message surface: base Chakra toast as the interim.** All messages emitted through **one** handler
  so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. Use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not
  the base hook. Marker comment naming SFCC-404 at the emit site.
  - Consequence (good): with a toast, the message **behaviour and copy** are delivered, so what's
    deferred is presentation only, not functionality. AC6 — whose entire observable outcome is the
    error message — becomes deliverable.
  - Word the Jira comment as *"message behaviour and copy delivered; surface deferred to SFCC-404"*,
    **not** "AC met" — the ACs say page-level banner and a toast is not one.
  - There is no cart override today, so the toast is being *implemented*, not inherited. Not free.
  - Chakra toasts portal to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement`. A Storybook `play` asserting a
    message must use `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing the portal exception —
    `testing.md` sanctions that specifically and nowhere else.
- **Guest auth: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, not a page
  redirect.** AC7 says "redirected to the login/registration page"; the drawer is a deliberate
  divergence. Backed by `cart.md` §2 CAI-008 (*"prompted to log in first"*), which is
  drawer-compatible; §4 CAI-018's "redirected to login" is the looser wording.
- **Pending item across auth: one hook instance, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'.`** The cart holds the
  pending line item in **React state** (covers the email-code and create-account routes, where the
  page never unloads) **and session storage** (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first,
  fall back to storage, clear both. Use the same 5-minute age bound as the hook's own intent so a
  stale item can't be resumed.
  - Rejected: one hook instance per line item (`intentId: cart-wishlist-${itemId}` would carry the
    product identity for free, but mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a
    drawer **per line item** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed
    priority).
  - Rejected for now: adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent`. It is the
    better long-term shape and the next multi-item caller will hit the same wall, but it changes a
    shared hook with three existing call sites. **Raise separately** with whoever owns that hook.
- **AC2 (empty state on removing the last item): not blocked.** Build a simple empty state now
  following the §2.14 precedent for structure and SFCC-315's Figma for visuals; SFCC-277 refines it
  later. Build it as a **discrete component, not inline JSX in the drawer**, so 277 is a swap in one
  file.
- **Jira: no AC edits.** PO-approved cards are not edited — document via a comment instead.
- **Disclosure of a silent change: explicitly out of scope** (Marcel, this session). Not to be
  re-raised.

# SFCC-11 Cart bundle — Phase 3 gate
**Stories:** SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 (Epic SFCC-11, Sprint 5, Squad-A, Marcel)
**Depth:** `exhaustive`
**Date:** 2026-09-16
**Note:** Jira, Figma (all 51 nodes) and the codebase were gathered conversationally across a long
session before this skill ran; the full record is `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/session-notes.md`
(§1–§11.11). This gate adds the sources that session did NOT cover — Confluence, the FED handbook,
`develop` currency, CODEOWNERS read directly, and the exemplar PRs — and re-verifies the rest.

## Gate table

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046) | **A `maxOrderQuantity` BM site preference IS the design** — Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site across all 8 storefronts — surfaced to the PWA as **`c_maxOrderQuantity`** on the SCAPI product response via hook `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET`. Resolution: product override (SFCC-703) → site preference → hardcoded 3. The TSD names SFCC-250 as a consumer and states the PWA fallback "should never be reached if the hook is correctly registered". **This contradicts the session's conclusion that no field exists and the constant is the implementation.** | 🟡 CLARIFY | Build 250 to read `c_maxOrderQuantity` with a fallback of 3 rather than promoting a shared constant. Degrades to today's behaviour when absent, picks up the real value when the hook ships. |
| 2 | Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` + Jira | The TSD is **`v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off `Pending`**, and its own template states a TSD is not approved for implementation until signed. **Jira SFCC-268 is nonetheless marked `Ready for SIT` (Done).** Live probe of the dev sandbox found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — consistent with the hook not being deployed. The TSD itself says "SFCC-196 and SFCC-250 are blocked — neither PDP nor Cart enforcement can be implemented without a config source." | 🟡 CLARIFY | Assumption to carry: 250 builds against the fallback and is **not verifiable end-to-end** until the hook is deployed. Marcel to decide whether that is acceptable or whether 268 needs reopening. |
| 3 | Confluence `04.1.5 Cart and Inventory` (302415874) | **CAI-035 states "disable the Checkout CTA and display an error identifying the out-of-stock item(s) … at checkout entry".** SFCC-275 AC3 states the CTA and express buttons "remain visually enabled but are blocked at backend level". | 🟡 CLARIFY | They reconcile only if "at checkout entry" means the block fires on the attempt rather than pre-emptively in the cart — which is what AC3 describes. Carry as a stated assumption; 275 builds the buttons enabled. |
| 4 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-017 | The requirement says **"an error message will be displayed if the customer attempts to exceed this limit"**. The Figma renders max-quantity with the **warning** variant (grey info icon, `text/subtlest`), and SFCC-250 AC4 says max-quantity explicitly does **not** block checkout. Requirement says error; design and AC say warning. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Follow the design + AC (warning). Assumption stated: "error" in CAI-017 means user-facing feedback, not the error severity tier. |
| 5 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-018 | The requirement says **"the system will redirect them to the login page"** — matching SFCC-272 AC7's wording. Marcel decided to use the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` instead. **Two sources say page.** The session justified the drawer partly on `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2's softer "prompted to log in first" — a paraphrase, weaker than this source. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Marcel's decision stands as a deliberate override (consistent with the four other auth-drawer surfaces), but the justification is weaker than presented. Record on the 272 comment as an override, not as an AC reading. |
| 6 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-001…005 | **Mini-Cart is confirmed OUT OF SCOPE** (all five rows, per Vicky Routley). Our components live in Figma frames named `cart/drawer`. The cards are titled "Cart **Page** – …". | 🔵 NOTE | Resolved by reading: Zimmermann's cart *page* is implemented as a drawer; the out-of-scope mini-cart is a separate, smaller overlay. Worth stating explicitly so nobody reads `cart/drawer` as the out-of-scope mini-cart. |
| 7 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-005 vs Figma | The Figma cart drawer contains a **`Recommended-for-you` rail (430×231)**. The only recommendations requirement, CAI-005, is a **Mini-Cart** row and is **out of scope**. So the rail in the cart drawer has no in-scope requirement behind it — and it is Einstein-powered, which is Not Deployed on all 8 sites. | 🔵 NOTE | Not in our 7 cards. Do not build it. Flag to whoever owns 816/274. |
| 8 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-033 | **"The system will not indicate split-shipment scenarios to the customer at cart level."** | 🟡 CLARIFY | Directly relevant to 250's per-line decision: when one SKU occupies two lines because of differing shipment, the shopper sees two identical-looking rows with **no explanation permitted**. Carry as a known UX consequence of per-line enforcement. |
| 9 | Confluence `04.1.5` CAI-030 | **"Low-stock messaging will not be displayed in the mini-cart or cart page."** | 🔵 NOTE | Constraint on 795's state set — no low-stock variant. |
| 10 | Confluence `04.9 Cart Order Summary` (453902337) | Per-storefront totals matrix. Shipping and Taxes rows are ❌ on the four Global-e sites (HK, ME, US Intl, EU Intl). Grand Total formula differs by region and is **⚠️ TBC on all four Global-e sites**. US free-shipping threshold **⚠️ TBC**. | 🔵 NOTE | Explains the three Grand Total variants (two hidden) found in Figma. Belongs to SFCC-274/816, not our 7. Confirms the "international" set that 275 AC2 branches on. |
| 11 | CODEOWNERS | **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has NO entry, and there is no catch-all rule.** So the five `item-variant` files — the half of the Option-B override with the **11-surface blast radius** — would merge with **no required code-owner review**. `product-item/` by contrast pulls in `@pwa-squad-b` + `@tier-2-approvers` + `@tier-1-approvers`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Either add an `item-variant/` CODEOWNERS entry (Tier 1 Governance change, separate ticket) or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned. Marcel to call. |
| 12 | Codebase / git | Local `develop` is **41 commits behind `origin/develop`**. The working branch `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` is 7 behind / 20 ahead and **carries open PR #112**. | 🔵 NOTE | `git checkout develop && git pull --ff-only` before cutting any branch. Do not branch from the current one. |
| 13 | Codebase / `typography.ts` | Our `caption` textStyle is **already `fontWeights.medium`**, matching Figma `Default/Caption-strong`. The gap is the reverse — Figma's **`Default/Caption` (regular/400, 12px)**, used for the inline error/warning text, has no counterpart (`body2` is regular but 14px). | 🟡 CLARIFY | Use `textStyle="caption"` with the weight overridden in the component's own recipe, annotated. **Avoids a Tier 1 change to `theme/foundation/typography.ts` from a cart ticket.** Raise `captionRegular` as a follow-up. |
| 14 | Codebase / PR #85 | SFCC-236 is the exact precedent: 45 files, atoms → molecules → organism, each with `index.tsx` + `index.test.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` + `<name>.css.ts` (some with `<name>.css.test.ts`), a **page-level mapper** (`productListCardMapper.ts` + test) converting SDK data to component props, shared constants at **`ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`**, theme registration, registry regen, and e2e split into sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders. | 🔵 NOTE | Follow it. Note it puts shared constants in `ui-kits/`, whereas `overrideStyling.md` documents `theme/components/` (`footerShared.ts`). Two precedents exist; `ui-kits/` is the newer. |
| 15 | FED handbook | Read for the override-interception and copy-first sections only. It cites `overrideStyling.md` 11 times and does not contradict it on anything this build touches. | 🔵 NOTE | Per the skill's own rule, `overrideStyling.md` wins where they differ. Nothing to reconcile here. **Local-only file — never citable in a PR, commit or code comment.** |
| 16 | qa.yml | There is **no `cart` e2e area**. `e2e-localhost` only runs when every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside one area's allow-list; otherwise it resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` and does not run. **Every cart PR currently gets no PR-time E2E.** | 🟡 CLARIFY | Add a `cart` allow-list group to `detect-changes` plus `@cart` tags. `.github/workflows/` is **Tier 1 CI/CD** — needs the Hard Rule #2 process. |
| 17 | Figma (session) | Design System 2026 file was **not** opened. Token mapping was instead resolved directly against `theme/foundation/` — every colour in the cart design already exists there (`grey`, `red[500]`, `green[500]`, `ivory[200]`), and every Figma named style maps to a registered textStyle bar the one in #13. | 🔵 NOTE | Declared, not silently skipped. The authority for what we may use is our own foundation, which was checked exhaustively. |
| 18 | Phase 2 reuse | `/feature-spec` and `/scope-check` were **not** run. Their input — a single scoped prompt to verdict — does not exist in this flow; the plan was produced across a full session and is far more specific than either emits. | 🔵 NOTE | Verdict restated directly instead: **SAFE-with-conditions.** No Tier 1 file is in the manifest (#13 avoids the one candidate). Tier 2 is entered deliberately at `product-item/`. The two real scope risks are #11 (ungoverned `item-variant/`) and #16 (Tier 1 CI change for the e2e area) — both named, neither silent. |

## Blockers
**None 🔴.** Nothing stops planning. Fourteen 🟡/🔵 items carry into the plan as stated assumptions
or notes.

## Assumptions the plan carries
1. 250 reads `c_maxOrderQuantity` with a fallback of 3, and is **not end-to-end verifiable** until
   the SFCC-268 hook is deployed (#1, #2).
2. CAI-035's "disable the Checkout CTA" is satisfied by a block on the checkout *attempt*, not a
   disabled button in the cart (#3).
3. CAI-017's "error message" means user-facing feedback, not the error severity tier; max-quantity
   renders as a **warning** (#4).
4. SFCC-272 AC7 is served by the existing auth **drawer**, as a deliberate override of two sources
   that say "login page" (#5).
5. The `cart/drawer` Figma frames are the cart **page**, not the out-of-scope mini-cart (#6).
6. Per-line max-quantity enforcement will occasionally show two visually identical rows with no
   explanation, because CAI-033 forbids surfacing split shipments at cart level (#8).
7. The regular-weight 12px caption is achieved by overriding weight in the component recipe rather

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	
4	const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';
5	
6	export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
7	  /**
8	   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
9	   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
10	   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
11	   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
12	   */
13	  variant: 'error' | 'warning';
14	  /**
15	   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
16	   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
17	   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
18	   * §11.2 exact copy).
19	   */
20	  text: string;
21	};
22	
23	/**
24	 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
25	 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
26	 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
27	 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
28	 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
29	 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
30	 *
31	 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
32	 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's quantity display
33	 * (zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx's own `<chakra.span __css={styles.value} aria-live="polite">`) —
34	 * so a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
35	 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
36	 *
37	 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
38	 */
39	export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
40	  const styles = useStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });
41	
42	  return (
43	    <chakra.p __css={styles} aria-live="polite" data-testid="zimm-inline-message">
44	      {text}
45	    </chakra.p>
46	  );
47	};
48

1	import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
5	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
6	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
7	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
8	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
9	 * type/colour.)
10	 *
11	 * Single visual node, no independent per-part state — `defineStyleConfig` + `useStyleConfig(...,
12	 * {variant})` (ZimmNavItem's / ZimmWishlistBadge's pattern) applies directly here, rather than
13	 * ZimmQuantityStepper's function-form `baseStyle` (which exists there because that recipe has
14	 * multiple PARTS needing independent values from one shared boolean, not a single Chakra-native
15	 * `variant` switch).
16	 *
17	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
18	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
19	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
20	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
21	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
22	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
23	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
24	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
25	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
26	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
27	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below to override the textStyle-expanded medium
28	 * value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied after the textStyle expansion
29	 * wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already
30	 * documents and relies on for the identical reason.
31	 *
32	 * `width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly, rather
33	 * than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default.
34	 *
35	 * No low-stock variant: a separate requirement explicitly forbids low-stock messaging at the
36	 * cart level (SFCC-795 §11.2 build decisions) — the variants map below only ever has the two
37	 * keys `error`/`warning`; do not add a third.
38	 */
39	const baseStyle = {
40	  textStyle: 'caption',
41	  fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
42	  width: 'full',
43	};
44	
45	const variants = {
46	  // Figma `text/error` #9c0000 -> status.error (session-notes.md §11.10(6) colour audit).
47	  error: {
48	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)',
49	  },
50	  // Figma `text/muted` / `text/subtlest` #969696 -> both collapse onto this one token, no
51	  // ambiguity in this codebase's own set (session-notes.md §11.10(6)).
52	  //
53	  // Max-quantity messaging ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") uses THIS variant,
54	  // not `error` — even though its own requirement/AC text uses the word "error" to describe it.
55	  // That word is describing "user-facing feedback" in the requirement's own vocabulary, not
56	  // asserting the error SEVERITY tier: the actual Figma design and that story's own AC agree the
57	  // rendered treatment is grey/warning, not red/error. Deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation,
58	  // settled at this build's planning gate — not a mistake, and not to be "corrected" back to
59	  // `error` by a future reader matching the word alone.
60	  warning: {
61	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)',
62	  },
63	};
64	
65	export const ZimmInlineMessage = defineStyleConfig({
66	  baseStyle,
67	  variants,
68	});

1	/*

4	 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

6	 */
7	
8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
12	 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
55	 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
56	 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
57	 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
58	 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
59	 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
60	 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
61	 *
62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 */
80	import React from 'react';
81	
82	// Chakra Components
83	import {
84	  Box,
85	  Fade,
86	  Flex,
87	  Stack,
88	  Text,
89	  useMultiStyleConfig,
90	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
91	
92	// Project Components
93	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
94	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
95	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
96	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
97	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
98	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
99	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
100	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
101	import ProductQuantityPicker from './product-quantity-picker';
102	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
103	
104	// Hooks
105	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
106	
107	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
108	
109	type SfccProduct = any;
110	
111	type ProductItemProps = {
112	  product: SfccProduct;
113	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
114	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
115	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
116	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
117	  /**
118	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
119	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
120	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
121	   */
122	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
123	  showLoading?: boolean;
124	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
125	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
126	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
127	  isRemoving?: boolean;
128	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
129	  /**
130	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
131	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
132	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
133	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
134	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
135	   */
136	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
137	  /**
138	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
139	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
140	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
141	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
142	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
143	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
144	   */
145	  message?: {
146	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
147	    text: string;
148	  };
149	};
150	
151	/**
152	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
153	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
154	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
155	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
156	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
157	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
158	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
159	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
160	 */
161	const ProductItem = ({
162	  product,
163	  primaryAction,
164	  secondaryActions,
165	  deliveryActions,
166	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
167	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
168	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
169	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
170	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
171	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
172	  showLoading = false,
173	  containerStyles = {},
174	  isRemoving = false,
175	  pickupInStore = false,
176	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
177	  message,
178	}: ProductItemProps) => {
179	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
180	    product,
181	    false,
182	    false,
183	    pickupInStore,
184	  );
185	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
186	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
187	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
188	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
189	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
190	  return (
191	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
192	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
193	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
194	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
195	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
196	            <CartItemVariantImage />
197	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
198	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
199	                <Stack spacing={1}>
200	                  <CartItemVariantName />
201	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
202	                  <HideOnDesktop>
203	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
204	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
205	                    </Box>
206	                  </HideOnDesktop>
207	                </Stack>
208	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
209	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
210	                )}
211	              </Flex>
212	
213	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
214	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
215	              )}
216	
217	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
218	                <Stack spacing={1}>
219	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
220	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
221	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
222	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
223	                    ) : (
224	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
225	                        product={product}
226	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
227	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
228	                        quantity={quantity}
229	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
230	                      />
231	                    ))}
232	                </Stack>
233	                <Stack>
234	                  <HideOnMobile>
235	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
236	                  </HideOnMobile>
237	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
238	                </Stack>
239	              </Flex>
240	
241	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
242	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
243	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
244	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
245	
246	              <Box>
247	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
248	                  <Fade in={true}>
249	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
250	                      {inventoryMessage}
251	                    </Text>
252	                  </Fade>
253	                )}
254	              </Box>
255	
256	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
257	            </Stack>
258	          </Flex>
259	
260	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
261	            <HideOnDesktop>
262	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
263	            </HideOnDesktop>
264	          )}
265	        </Stack>
266	      </ItemVariantProvider>
267	    </Box>
268	  );
269	};
270	
271	export default ProductItem;
272

/**
 * Recipe guards — regression tests for four failure modes that reached a feature branch
 * despite passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run.
 *
 * All four share a shape: the value is a *valid* `SystemStyleObject` entry, so TypeScript is
 * satisfied; no lint rule covers it; and nothing asserts layout. Each one renders plausible,
 * wrong output that is only visible by opening the page.

 *   1. A spacing-scale key on a sizing property. Chakra resolves `width`/`height`/`boxSize`
 *      through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as
 *      `space` only (deliberately — see foundation/sizes.ts), so `width: 'xl'` silently reads
 *      Chakra's default `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
 *
 *   2. The same trap on a typography property. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are
 *      deliberately NOT registered either (theme/index.ts explains why), so a bare key reads
 *      Chakra's default or resolves to nothing at all. See TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS below.
 *
 *   3. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
 *      `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does
 *      not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base
 *      properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand
 *      can silently reset a longhand the base declared earlier.
 *
 *   4. A bare scale key inside a compound shorthand. Chakra resolves a token only when it is
 *      the entire value; `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim, the browser rejects the
 *      declaration, and the padding does not apply at all.
 *
 * A fifth guard below (`no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered
 * scale`) is a different kind of check — not a wrong-value bug, since `space` and `colors`
 * ARE registered Chakra scales (theme/index.ts), so a bare key there resolves to the correct
 * Zimmermann value either way. It enforces a house style instead: override components must
 * always reference a zimm value via `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`, never a
 * bare Chakra token string, so a PR reviewer sees an unambiguous zimm reference at every call
 * site instead of having to recall which scales are and are not registered.
 *

 * `theme`). They cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop on a component — there is a
 * live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`
 * (`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing) that no test here can reach. Catching that class needs

 * house-style guard has the same JSX blind spot — `footerNavColumn/index.tsx` had a bare
 * `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in an inline `sx` merge (not a recipe) that this test cannot see;
 * it was only found by a manual grep across `overrides/app/components/`, not by this suite.
 */

content.content:
/**
 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
 *
 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
 *
 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
 *
 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
 * walks the component source.
 *
 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
 *
 * It is not a whole-repo guard, and nothing else covers the remainder: the model is strictly
 * sibling-based (a recipe's `parts` are reconciled against the `index.tsx` beside it), so a
 * recipe that does not sit next to its component is out of reach. `theme/components/header.ts`
 * is the only multipart recipe in that position today and is therefore unguarded.
 * `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` does not pick it up either — that suite has no
 * parts-vs-reads check of any kind; it guards bare token keys and recipe namespacing.
 *
 * `READ_RE` recognises only the identifier `styles`, so a second binding in the same component
 * is invisible here: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` reads `chrome.actions`. That one is
 * deliberately out of scope rather than a gap to close — `chrome` holds *ZimmModal's* recipe,
 * so the sibling model would misattribute `actions` to `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts`, which
 * correctly does not declare it.
 */

import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const COMPONENTS = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'overrides/app/components');
